b: ^ "We have spoken about the missed delivery. Let us leave the account honest."
^"I remember waiting for the provisions. What happened?"
^"The provisions delivery was called off. There is still ordinary work and conversation to be had."
^The merchant turns a cracked cup in his hands. "You told me the spring has fallen silent. I should stop promising thirsty travelers a drink."
^The merchant shades his stall with a woven cloth. "A little honest work leaves the evening free for wonders."

greeting: ^Tell him you cannot keep the delivery commitment.
^Ask if your reliable help has earned another small favor.

b: ^"You found the side passage yourself? Then you know more than the men who sell directions to it."
^"They say a narrow passage beyond the workshop leads to a spring that sings after sunset. I heard it from a boatman; I have never tasted its water."

c-1: ^"The courier needs provisions. Bring the agreed goods before the deadline; the payment is set aside."
c-2: ^"Find the courier during working hours. The workshop bench is yours to use, but a deadline waits for no oven."
c-3: ^"The courier spoke well of you. Reliable hands are worth more than loud promises."
c-5: ^"Dust in the channel, you say? Then I owe that boatman a question. I will tell travelers to carry their own water. Thank you for checking instead of repeating me."
c-6: ^"Better to warn me than leave the courier waiting. I will release the reserved payment. We can still trade as neighbors."
c-7: ^"Thank you for saying so. I remember the missed parcel, but an honest word matters. There is no fine and no door closed to you."
c-8: ^"You kept your word on the provisions. Could you take four measures of grain to the courier as well? This is optional; the usual trade remains open."
c-9: ^"Two commitments kept. I know whose hands I can trust with a small errand."
